finding: INV-4 / §3 rule 5 VIOLATED (verified by running the real function): spliceTranscript's blank-transcript branch collapses the seam UNCONDITIONALLY, including when the span being removed is ZERO-LENGTH (i.e. nothing was ever written there). The first interim decode commonly returns empty — the design's own §2 measurement shows toolbarCaption=null at t+1.2s — and the engine writes it via writeDictation(session, normalizeInterimTranscript(null)) => spliceTranscript(value, anchor{12,12}, ""). On the design's own repro draft "Please book  for next Tuesday." caret 12, this silently rewrites the user's untouched draft to "Please book for next Tuesday." — one whitespace char destroyed before a single word was dictated. Cancel CANNOT undo it: the session span is now zero-length with anchorText=="", so relocateSpan returns {12,12} and restoreSpan is a no-op, leaving the composer NOT byte-for-byte as it was. Same loss occurs on the interim-shrink path (non-empty write then a blank decode) and persists through a No-speech-detected commit. The collapse is only sound when removing text this session actually wrote; it must be gated on span.end > span.start (or on written !== "").

§5 detach rule + §3 rule 7 VIOLATED: cancelRecording computes restored = dictation.anchor and passes it to focusComposer UNCONDITIONALLY, including when the session DETACHED. restoreDictation() correctly returns early for a detached session ("restores nothing — that text is the user's now"), but focusComposer then still runs store.applyEdit(getText(), anchor.start, anchor.end), SELECTING an arbitrary range of the user's own text at the pre-recording offsets. Reachable state: caret/selection anchor {5,8} on "call Bob tomorrow", interims replace it, the user edits inside the provisional span (detach), then Cancel — the composer ends focused with 3 characters of the USER's text selected, and the next keystroke deletes them. Data-destructive. TEST-16's detach case asserts only textarea.value and never selectionStart/End, so it is green on this.

HOLLOW ACCEPTANCE TEST for INV-5. TEST-19 manufactures the no-caret state with Object.defineProperty(el,'selectionStart',{get:()=>null}) — a value a mounted <textarea> NEVER returns (verified in Chromium: a never-focused textarea whose value was set via el.value=draft, exactly what TextInput's draft-restore effect does, reports selectionStart === value.length; only a textarea whose content came from markup reports 0). Production readSelection() therefore never yields null for a mounted composer, so the entire selection===null branch (insertTranscript's append path, resolveWriteSpan's `?? {value.length,value.length}`, currentCaret's `??`, the anchorText ternary) is unreachable in shipped code, and the REAL never-focused path is not exercised by any test. If the genuine no-caret behaviour regressed (e.g. readSelection started returning {0,0} explicitly, putting dictation at the FRONT of the draft) TEST-19 would still pass. Its companion unit acceptance TEST-6 (voiceLogic.test.ts:~228) has the same defect: it pins a pure-function input production cannot produce.

§3 rule 5 ("the original caret/selection restored") half-implemented on the shifted-span path: restoreDictation relocates the span and applies the CORRECT restored selection via applyEdit(edit.value, edit.start, edit.end), and focusComposer then immediately OVERWRITES it with the STALE anchor offsets. Reachable: user has "Bob" selected at {5,8}, dictation replaces it, the user types "XY" at position 0 during recording (shifting everything by 2), then cancels — the value is restored byte-for-byte but the re-selection lands on {5,8} instead of {7,10}, selecting the wrong three characters. focusComposer should re-select what restoreDictation actually restored, not the anchor. TEST-14/TEST-21 never type before the span, so both are green.

INV-1's "NO transcript text is rendered in the composer toolbar" clause is certified only by assertions that cannot fail. (a) expect(byTestId(page,'voice-live-caption')).toHaveCount(0) is a tautology — the element was deleted from source, so no implementation of this feature could ever make it non-zero; it is repeated 4x across the 14-voice specs. (b) The toolbar text assertion uses page.locator('[data-testid="chat-input-toolbar"], [role="group"]'): `chat-input-toolbar` does not exist anywhere in the repo (grepped), and the only [role="group"] in this flow is MicButton's recording chrome, which is UNMOUNTED by the time the assertion runs (after stopDictation). allInnerTexts() on an empty match set yields [] and join(' ') yields '', so not.toContain('a table') passes vacuously. A regression that re-rendered the transcript in the toolbar WHILE recording would not be caught. Assert the toolbar's text mid-recording against a real, existing container.

§3 framing "Dictation is an editor input" is not honoured by the persistence layer: applyComposerEdit (and setMessage) write el.value directly and dispatch no input/change event, and setDraft() is called ONLY from TextInput.handleInput (onChange, TextInput.tsx:119). Dictated text therefore never enters the draft store. Because this change makes dictation the composer's primary content producer (a per-second stream plus the whole final transcript) rather than one append at Stop, the consequence is now material: dictate, then switch conversation A->B->A and TextInput's restore effect writes the STALE stored draft back over the textarea — the entire transcript is silently lost. Either dispatch a native input event after applyComposerEdit or call setDraft from the applier.

Cross-pane corruption escalated by the offset-based rewrite: ownerTextStore(paneId) silently falls back to Chat.$.TextStore — the FOCUSED pane — when paneRegistry.get(paneId) is undefined, and unregisterPane() deletes the handle on pane unmount (chatBridge.ts:38). An interim tick (~1s timer) or a restoreDictation firing after the recording pane closes therefore applies ABSOLUTE offsets computed against pane A's draft to pane B's composer: spliceTranscript/restoreSpan will delete or overwrite an arbitrary [start,end) range of another conversation's draft. Pre-change the same fallback only appended a stray transcript; it can now destroy text. Resolve the owning store once and BAIL (rather than falling back) when the owning pane is gone.

§3 rule 7 ("the user's own typing always wins") is implemented only for SPAN ownership, not for CARET ownership. writeDictation calls store.applyEdit(edit.value, edit.caret) on EVERY interim tick, unconditionally moving the composer's caret to the end of the dictated words even when the user's caret is elsewhere and they are actively typing. Reachable state ("the user typing during dictation"): with live captions on, a user editing at position 3 while dictation writes at position 50 has their caret yanked ~once per second, so their subsequent keystrokes land INSIDE the dictated span — which then trips relocateSpan into detaching. Rule 7 requires the write to leave the caret alone when the current selection is outside the span being rewritten.

INV-2 ("real time transcribe") is gated behind a control whose user-facing name now describes a surface this change DELETED. The toggle's tooltip and aria-label are still "Turn live captions on/off" and the store field is still liveCaptions, but with the toolbar caption strip removed the switch's only remaining effect is whether dictation streams into the chat input at all. A user who has (or turns) it off gets no real-time transcription and no way to discover that from the label. Rename the affordance (and ideally the state field) to what it now controls, e.g. "Live dictation".

§5 mechanism divergence between the captions-ON and captions-OFF paths: with live captions off the session never writes, so session.span stays null and commitTranscript skips the session entirely, inserting at store.getSelection() (the caret at STOP time) rather than at session.anchor (the caret at RECORD time) that §5 specifies as the first write target. Defensible under rule 7 and documented in the function's own docstring, but it means the same feature has two different insertion-point semantics depending on a preference toggle, and only the captions-OFF one is covered (TEST-15 case 2 never moves the caret during recording, so the two are indistinguishable there).

Behaviour outside the design's stated contract, untested: fail() now calls restoreDictation()+endDictation(), so a transcription FAILURE after interims silently deletes the words the user watched appear. INV-4 enumerates cancelled / superseded / unmounted — not failed; §3 rule 5 likewise. Discarding a recording's visible output on a backend error is a real user-data decision (the audio is gone, the words are gone) that no rule in the design authorises and no test in TESTS.md exercises (no spec drives a /transcribe error after interim writes). Either record it as a decision in the design doc or keep the provisional words and surface the error alongside them.

cancelRecording re-selects the STALE anchor. restoreDictation() (line 236-244) already applies the CORRECT restored span via applyEdit(edit.value, edit.start, edit.end); cancelRecording then sets `restored = dictation.anchor` (the offsets captured at record START) and focusComposer (line 735) re-applies applyEdit(getText(), anchor.start, anchor.end) in a rAF, overwriting the correct selection with stale offsets. REPRODUCED: draft 'call Bob tomorrow' with 'Bob' selected (5..8), interim writes 'Alice Smith', user then types 'AB' at index 0, cancel -> value correctly 'ABcall Bob tomorrow' but the selection is 5..8 = 'l B' instead of 7..10 = 'Bob'. Violates the documented INV-4 'cancel leaves the composer exactly as it was'. TEST-14 in DictationComposer.test.tsx and TEST-21 in dictation-caret-insert.spec.ts both only exercise the no-shift case, so neither catches it. Fix: return the span restoreDictation actually restored instead of dictation.anchor (or drop the redundant re-apply in focusComposer).

ownerTextStore() silently falls back to `Chat.$.TextStore` (the FOCUSED pane) whenever paneRegistry.get(paneId) misses. Before this change that fallback was consulted ONCE, at final commit; the dictation session now calls it on EVERY interim tick, on restoreDictation and on commitTranscript. REPRODUCED with two composers (pane A recording, pane B focused): unregistering pane A mid-recording leaves A's provisional words 'hello there' permanently STRANDED (cancel restores nothing because relocateSpan fails against B's text -> the session silently detaches), and Stop writes the authoritative 'FINAL TRANSCRIPT' into PANE B's composer at PANE B's caret. That is a cross-pane write of dictated content plus an INV-4 violation. A missing owning pane should abort the write, not redirect it to whichever pane happens to be focused.

spliceTranscript's blank-transcript branch runs its seam-collapse even when the span is COLLAPSED (start === end), so a write that removes nothing still DELETES one of the user's characters. REPRODUCED end-to-end: draft 'hello  world' with the caret at 6 (between the two spaces), live captions on, one interim decode returning '' -> composer becomes 'hello world'; cancelRecording does NOT put the space back (restoreDictation relocates the zero-length span and restores the empty anchorText), so INV-4 'byte-exact restore' is false. Guard the collapse on start !== end (nothing was removed => nothing to collapse). The unit suite tests the blank branch only with a NON-empty span (voiceLogic.test.ts:83), so it passes.

focusComposer defers a frame and then re-reads the store, with no epoch/generation check. REPRODUCED: after stopRecording commits the transcript, replacing the composer value before the rAF fires (the conversation-switch case -- TextInput is REUSED across an in-app A->B switch and its draft-restore effect writes el.value directly) leaves the rAF applying the STALE caret offset (19) into the NEW draft and focusing it. The value itself is not clobbered (it re-writes store.getText()), so the harm is a wrong caret plus an unrequested focus steal into a different conversation's composer. It is also reachable from the MicButton unmount cleanup (MicButton.tsx:69-73), which calls cancelRecording -> focusComposer while the component is going away.

The harness comment 'A fresh engine per test: voiceEngine memoizes on the get identity, so a new get closure yields a new engine with clean module-scope session state' is FALSE. dictation, requestGeneration, mediaRecorder, chunks, finalizing, and every timer are MODULE scope in _engine.ts, shared by all engine instances; only errorRevertTimer is per-instance. REPRODUCED: engine A recording, then a second engine built exactly as beforeEach builds it -> B's startRecording overwrites A's `dictation` with no restore, so A's streamed words are stranded and B's cancel restores only B's span. The tests currently pass only because afterEach's cancelRecording tears the shared state down; the comment will mislead the next author into assuming isolation that does not exist.

Vacuous assertion. `page.locator('[data-testid="chat-input-toolbar"], [role="group"]').allInnerTexts()` -- the testid `chat-input-toolbar` does not exist ANYWHERE in the repo (verified by grep over src/ and sdk/), and the only relevant [role="group"] is MicButton's recording wrapper, which is unmounted by the time this runs (after Stop). An empty locator yields [], so `[].join(' ')` is '' and `not.toContain('a table')` passes unconditionally. The prose 'NOTHING transcript-shaped is rendered in the composer toolbar' is therefore unverified by this spec.

The diff replaces a `voice-live-caption` count-0 assertion with `expect(byTestId(page,'chat-message-textarea')).toHaveValue('')` under the comment '...and nothing dictation-shaped reached the composer either'. The test is the UNPERMITTED-user case: it never types, never records, and no mic affordance exists, so the composer is empty for reasons unrelated to dictation. Trivially true; would pass with the whole feature reverted.

`expect(byTestId(page,'voice-live-caption')).toHaveCount(0)` (also at dictation-caret-insert.spec.ts:113 and live-captions-stream.spec.ts:76,82) asserts the absence of an element this same diff DELETED from MicButton.tsx. It can never fail again and is not a guard against a transcript re-appearing in the toolbar -- any future toolbar transcript would use a different element. A meaningful guard would assert on the toolbar's rendered text, which the one spec that tries (dictation-caret-insert.spec.ts:114) does vacuously.

Composer spans are raw UTF-16 code-unit offsets with no surrogate-pair guard, so an offset landing inside a surrogate pair splits the code point. REPRODUCED: spliceTranscript('a\u{1F44D}b', {start:1,end:2}, 'X') -> 'a X \udc4db' (a lone low surrogate, rendered as a replacement glyph); spliceTranscript with a caret at index 2 (inside the pair) -> 'a\ud83d X \udc4db'. Not obviously reachable through the UI (browsers clamp mouse/keyboard selection to code-point boundaries), but applyComposerEdit's setSelectionRange does no such clamping, so an arithmetic caret could produce one. Low, defensive.

clampIndex maps NaN/Infinity/-Infinity to `value.length`, i.e. a corrupt or unreadable selection silently degrades to APPEND-AT-END -- the exact behaviour this feature exists to eliminate -- with nothing logged. Verified: spliceTranscript('abc',{start:NaN,end:NaN},'X') === spliceTranscript('abc',{start:Infinity,...}) === 'abc X'. Repo rule 6 (never silently swallow a real failure) argues for distinguishing 'no insertion point' (the legitimate null case, already modelled) from 'a garbage insertion point'.

applyComposerEdit (and setMessage) write el.value directly and never dispatch an input/change event, so TextInput's onChange handler (handleInput -> setDraft, TextInput.tsx:117-120) never runs for dictated text. A dictated transcript is therefore NEVER persisted to the per-conversation draft, and TextInput's draft-restore effect (TextInput.tsx:112, `el.value = getDraft(draftKey)`) silently overwrites it on the next conversation switch. Pre-existing in class for the old setText-based append, but this change routes far more text (every interim tick plus the final commit) through the same unpersisted path.

fail() unconditionally restores + clears the module-scope `dictation`, but ONE fail() call site runs BEFORE the exclusive recording lock is acquired: startRecording's `if (!isRecordingSupported()) { fail(...) }` at line 461-464 sits above acquireRecordingLock at 469. On that path a live session belonging to ANOTHER pane would be restored (wiping its streamed words) and cleared. Latent only because isRecordingSupported() is a static per-browser predicate that cannot be false for one pane and true for another; still, fail()'s session cleanup should be conditional on this pane owning the session (e.g. dictation.gen === this request's gen, or recordingPaneId match).

acquireRecordingLock(null) returns true UNCONDITIONALLY ('single-pane: no cross-pane exclusion needed'), so a startRecording() with paneId === null bypasses exclusion entirely even while another pane holds the lock -- and then overwrites the module-scope `dictation`, mediaRecorder, chunks and timers of that in-flight recording. The invariant the DictationSession doc-comment relies on ('the exclusive recording lock guarantees at most one pane is in the recording flow at a time') therefore has a hole. Latent because MicButton only passes null when it renders outside a ChatPaneContext, which does not co-occur with split panes today.

focusComposer's guard was narrowed from `typeof document === 'undefined' || typeof requestAnimationFrame === 'undefined'` to just the rAF check, and on that branch it returns having done NOTHING -- no focus and, more importantly, no caret/selection restore. In any environment without rAF the post-stop caret placement and the post-cancel re-selection are silently skipped with no synchronous fallback. Cheap fix: fall back to calling the body inline instead of returning.
